# Testing Strategy

## Purpose

Design a coherent, risk-based testing approach for a project, feature or system before implementation and release practices become ad hoc.

## When to Use

- At project or feature start when the test approach is not yet explicit.
- When unit, integration and end-to-end responsibilities need to be separated.
- When CI test stages, coverage expectations or test ownership need to be defined.
- When integration boundaries or critical user journeys need deliberate coverage.

## When Not to Use

- To write individual test classes or test cases.
- To review an implementation for general code quality; use `development.code-review`.
- To treat line coverage as a substitute for behavior and risk coverage.

## Required Inputs

- System or feature scope and major components.
- Highest-risk behavior and failure impact.
- Deployment cadence, CI constraints and team context.
- Existing test tooling and known coverage when available.

## Working Method

1. Identify critical behavior, integration boundaries and failure modes.
2. Classify each risk into an appropriate test layer: unit, integration, contract or end-to-end.
3. Keep the fastest and most isolated checks closest to the implementation.
4. Reserve expensive end-to-end tests for critical journeys and boundary confidence.
5. Select tooling that fits the stack and can run reproducibly in CI.
6. Define measurable coverage expectations tied to risk rather than a universal percentage.
7. Define test-data, fixture and cleanup strategy.
8. Define ownership, execution cadence and failure-handling expectations.

## Decision Rules

- Higher-risk behavior requires stronger and usually multi-layer coverage.
- Prefer deterministic lower-level tests when they prove the same behavior reliably.
- A coverage metric is evidence, not the objective itself.
- External-system boundaries need explicit contract or integration coverage.
- A strategy that cannot run within the delivery cadence must be simplified or split into fast and extended suites.

## Output Requirements

Provide:
- system and risk summary;
- recommended test layers and scope per layer;
- tooling choices with rationale;
- coverage and quality expectations;
- CI execution plan;
- test-data approach;
- ownership and maintenance responsibilities.

## Quality Gates

- Critical behavior is mapped to at least one meaningful test layer.
- Integration boundaries are explicitly covered.
- End-to-end scope is intentionally limited to valuable journeys.
- Coverage expectations are measurable and risk-based.
- Test data and cleanup are addressed.
- CI duration is compatible with the delivery cadence.
- Responsibilities are explicit.

## Anti-patterns

- Inverting the test pyramid with many fragile end-to-end tests and few fast tests.
- Targeting 100% line coverage without meaningful assertions.
- Testing internal implementation details instead of observable behavior.
- Omitting test-data management and accepting flaky shared-state tests.

## Examples

- Define the test approach for a new REST API with unit, contract and integration coverage.
- Create a release test strategy for a Salesforce-to-ERP integration.
- Reduce an oversized end-to-end suite by moving deterministic checks to lower layers.
